For new fans of Twenty One Pilots, I would personally recommend listening to Vessel first. It's quite representative of the band's sound, and is more stylistically unified than their newest release. And of course, I would also recommend saving Regional At Best for last; there's a few songs from Vessel on there in rawer forms, and is also the hardest to find. It's definitely great, but more appealing to the hardcore fan.

Also important, know going in that Twenty One Pilots' schizoid pop style lends itself to many different types of songwriting and crosses genres often. There's a large amount of instrumental variety, and Tyler Joseph often switches between rapping, screaming and melodic singing. It is entirely possible that you will DISLIKE them on your first listen. While it is entirely up to you, I would advise giving them more than one shot...it's made me a devoted fan. I vividly remember hating Holding On To You when I heard it on the radio, and now it's one of my favorite songs.
